plans.note: No liability article surfaced in the outline, but the visible outline is partial (only 1.4, 5.4 and the body wrapper are exposed). Scan the unnumbered body text under sec-p0001 for any limitation, disclaimer or consequential-damages waiver; assess mutuality of any cap and the standard carve-outs (IP infringement, confidentiality, gross negligence/wilful misconduct). Treat as missing only if nothing appears in the full text.

Missing-type rule. Look through the body (sec-p0001) for any HDI indemnity covering third-party IP claims arising from the site development/hosting work and HDI's own negligence or misconduct, and for any reciprocal indemnity we owe on Deerskin Products content. If absent, flag as missing rather than redlining an existing clause.

Presence rule. Check Article 1 (site development scope, including sec-1.4 access provisions) and the body for any restriction on the Company operating competing catalogue/e-commerce channels or sourcing Deerskin Products elsewhere. Only a restriction binding us is in scope; restrictions on HDI benefit us and should not be flagged.

Presence rule with real likelihood here: a hosting/site development deal of this type often names HDI as sole developer/host for the Deerskin Products site. Review the Article 1 scope language and sec-1.4 for sole-source or exclusive-provider wording binding the Company, and confirm whether an exit or carve-out for other suppliers exists.

Direction rule. Search the fee/pricing provisions in the body for any obligation on the Company to extend HDI its best or most-favourable terms; an MFN running in our favour is welcome and must not be flagged.

Presence rule. Section 5.4 deals with each party appointing a representative, so personnel covenants may sit nearby; check for any non-solicit or no-hire binding the Company, its duration, scope of covered employees, and whether general advertising/unsolicited applicants are carved out.

The defined term 'Termination Date' confirms termination machinery exists in the unexposed text. Locate it in the body and test whether the Company may terminate on notice without penalty or termination fee, and whether HDI has a symmetrical or broader convenience right mid-term (which we resist).

Check the term provisions associated with 'Termination Date' for auto-renewal, the length of any renewal period, the non-renewal notice window (we prefer 30 days or less) and any price uplift. A missing uplift cap is a rationale note only, not a deviation.

Boilerplate is not itemised in the visible outline; expect governing law/venue in the miscellaneous provisions within sec-p0001. New York is likely given both parties' profile and would be compliant; Delaware, California or England and Wales are also accepted. Foreign arbitration would be the deviation.

Look in the miscellaneous provisions for the assignment clause. Confirm we may assign to affiliates and to a successor by merger or asset sale without HDI consent, and that HDI has no termination right triggered by our change of control. Note that HDI and the Company are affiliated entities, which may explain permissive drafting.

Central to a site development and hosting deal. Examine Article 1 (including sec-1.4 access to HDI systems) and the body for ownership of the developed site, code, look-and-feel, customer/order data and Deerskin Products content. Flag any vesting of our data or paid-for deliverables in HDI; ownership in our favour is not to be flagged.

Section 1.4 grants the Company access to HDI systems and is the primary licence-type grant. Test scope: whether affiliates and our contractors may use the access, whether it is revocable at will or suspendable, and whether it runs for the full term. Also check any reciprocal licence we grant HDI in our marks and content for over-breadth.

Parametric rule but audit rights against the customer are uncommon in a hosting arrangement; more likely the recordkeeping/reconciliation provisions run in our favour. Scan the body for any HDI right to inspect our records or premises, and if present check notice, frequency, business-hours limits and who bears cost.

Direction rule. Check the fee and termination provisions for liquidated damages, stipulated penalties, early-termination charges or interest-plus-penalty on late payment payable by the Company. Service credits or performance credits running to us are favourable and must not be flagged.

Look for HDI warranties on the development work and hosting services (workmanlike performance, conformity to specifications, uptime) and for the remedy and its duration. Note any 'AS IS' or blanket disclaimer of implied warranties, which would fail the fallback.

Missing-type rule. HDI hosts the site and handles order and customer data, so the rule is engaged. Search the body for commercial general liability, errors and omissions/technology, and cyber coverage plus certificate and additional-insured mechanics; if none, report as missing.

Presence rule. Review the fee/compensation provisions for minimum spend, guaranteed order volumes, minimum hosting fees or take-or-pay obligations on the Company, and whether any such commitment is paired with a termination or true-down right.

Missing-type rule tied to the 'Termination Date' machinery. Check the post-termination provisions for return or export of site content, customer and order data in usable format, migration/transition assistance, and any HDI right to withhold data pending payment. If no such provision exists, report as missing.
